import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    target = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()

    # Get watermark high_ts (single row)
    if len(watermark) > 0:
        high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    else:
        high_ts = pd.NaT

    # 1. Keep only events with event_ts > watermark.high_ts
    if pd.notna(high_ts):
        cdc = cdc[cdc["event_ts"] > high_ts]
    else:
        # if no watermark value, treat all events as new
        pass

    # 2. Per product_id, apply the LATEST event by (event_ts, event_seq)
    if len(cdc) > 0:
        cdc_sorted = cdc.sort_values(
            by=["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
            ascending=[True, True, True]
        )
        latest = cdc_sorted.groupby("product_id", as_index=False).tail(1)
    else:
        latest = cdc.copy()

    # Build target snapshot indexed by product_id for easy update
    target_indexed = target.set_index("product_id", drop=False)

    # Process each latest event per product
    for _, row in latest.iterrows():
        pid = row["product_id"]
        op = row["op"]
        if op == "D":
            if pid in target_indexed.index:
                target_indexed = target_indexed.drop(index=pid)
        else:
            # Upsert
            new_row = {
                "product_id": pid,
                "name": row["name"],
                "price": row["price"],
                "last_event_ts": row["event_ts"],
            }
            if pid in target_indexed.index:
                target_indexed.loc[pid, "name"] = new_row["name"]
                target_indexed.loc[pid, "price"] = new_row["price"]
                target_indexed.loc[pid, "last_event_ts"] = new_row["last_event_ts"]
            else:
                new_df = pd.DataFrame([new_row])
                new_df = new_df.set_index("product_id", drop=False)
                target_indexed = pd.concat([target_indexed, new_df])

    result = target_indexed.reset_index(drop=True)

    # Ensure column order and types match schema
    result = result[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]]
    result["product_id"] = result["product_id"].astype("int64")
    result["price"] = result["price"].astype("float64")
    result["last_event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(result["last_event_ts"])

    return {"new_snapshot": result}
